messages.author: 275c19e248701192
messages.subject: R is painfully slow
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to run SEM in lavaan and using bootstrapping. It usually takes long for the output to come but recently even after 6 to 7 hours I see no output. R console shows the red "Stop" sign indicating it is processing. Can anyone tell me what could be the problem and how may I resolve it?

Thanks in advance,

Regards,
Mahima

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: R is painfully slow
parts:
How many bootstrap samples are you running?

How long does it take a single model to converge?

Try 'manually' bootstrapping - use the sample() function to sample your data with replacement a few times and run the model on that - does it occasionally take a long time?

You can use the boot package to run a smaller number of bootstraps to give you an idea.

Sometimes though, you just need to wait. Set it running, go home, come back and hope it's finished. :)

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: R is painfully slow
parts: On Thu, 22 Nov 2018 at 10:23, <car...@web.de> wrote:
Jeremy, true. But it's also true that the bootstrap procedure is extremely slow when you compare it to Amos. I don't know why that is so.

I would guess because Amos is written in something like C++ (or perhaps Java), and lavaan is written in R is much slower than compiled languages.. Amos has IBM behind it, who have over 300,000 full time employees, when a general function works sub-optimally, they can rewrite it specifically for Amos. Lavaan has one person (who has a full time job, not writing Lavaan, and some contributors who also have real jobs). 

Lavaan relies on other functions For example, Lavaan has the  numDeriv package as a dependency, written by other people who might not even know that it is used in Lavaan, and want their functions to work in a general way for lots of people - they are not going to write their function in a way that specifically makes if fast for lavaan. 

The surprising (to me) thing about lavaan isn't that it runs slowly, the surprising thing is that it runs at all. :) .

Jeremy

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: R is painfully slow
parts:
On 11/22/18 7:23 PM, car...@web.de wrote:
> Jeremy, true. But it's also true that the bootstrap procedure is
> extremely slow when you compare it to Amos. I don't know why that is so.

My guess would be that Amos is using a single-iteration bootstrap. This
means that, instead of fully estimating the model again for each new
bootstrap sample (what lavaan is doing), only a single (Gauss)-Newton
step is taken, and then it stops. Obviously, this is much much faster.
And there are some theoretical arguments to justify this approach, but
my own findings are that the quality of the results is better with the
full bootstrap.

Tip: use verbose = TRUE, and then you can see what is going on.

Yves.

messages.author: 5abdb409f213d464
messages.subject: Re: R is painfully slow
parts:
Hi Yves et al.,

I can't imagine that, even though it may be true. But then I wouldn't understand this table: http://amosdevelopment.com/webhelp/summaryofbootstrapiterations1.htm

What I found, though, is this: "Amos uses the parameter estimates from the original sample as initial estimates in the iterative estimation procedure for each bootstrap sample. An alternative procedure, not implemented in Amos, would be to repeat for each bootstrap sample the same procedure for choosing initial values that was used in the analysis of the original sample" (http://amosdevelopment.com/webhelp/index.html?initialvaluesforthebootstrap.htm).
